            When it looks broken and is not

            (no output)
            Most commands say nothing at all when they work — cd, mkdir, touch, git add, git remote add. Silence is the success message. Do not ask “did something appear?”; ask did an error appear?
            (END)
            Your prompt is gone and typing does nothing. git log opened a pager. Press q. Arrow keys scroll. Nothing is frozen.
            a full-screen editor
            git revert and a bare git commit open vim. Esc, then :wq, then Return accepts and leaves. Or avoid it: --no-edit, or -m "message".
            remote origin already exists
            You ran git remote add twice. That error means it worked the first time. Carry on.
            command not found
            The program is almost certainly installed; your terminal just does not know where it is. Not a missing program — a missing path.
            push done, site unchanged
            A git push takes seconds; publishing does not, and your terminal is told nothing about it. Watch the repo page for the green tick. GitHub says up to ten minutes.

            Terminal

            pwd
            Where am I? Prints a path.
            ls
            What is in here? Prints names — or nothing, if the folder is empty, which is also success.
            ls -a
            The same, including hidden files like .gitignore and .env.
            cd foldername
            Go into it. Silent — but your prompt changes.
            cd ..
            Go up one level.
            mkdir foldername
            Make a folder. Silent.
            touch file.js
            Make an empty file. Silent.
            code .
            Open this folder in VS Code — the folder, never the single file. Silent; a window opens.
            ↑ and Tab
            Up-arrow recalls the last command; Tab completes a name you have half-typed. Use both constantly.

            git — the daily loop

            git status
            What has changed, and what is staged. Run it more often than you think you need to.
            git add .
            Stage everything changed. Silent — check with git status.
            git commit -m "msg"
            Save a snapshot. Prints the short hash and how many files changed.
            git push
            Send commits to GitHub. Prints a few progress lines and the two hashes.
            git pull
            Bring down commits made elsewhere. Do this before starting work if you ever push from two machines.
            git log --oneline -10
            The last ten commits, one line each — and no pager, so you keep your prompt.

            git — branches and undo

            git checkout -b name
            Make a branch and move to it. “Switched to a new branch”.
            git checkout main
            Move to an existing branch. No -b — that is the difference.
            git merge name
            Bring that branch into this one.
            git merge --abort
            A conflict you do not want to deal with right now. Silent, and you are exactly back where you were.
            git revert <hash> --no-edit
            Undo a commit that other people may already have, by adding a new commit that reverses it. Safe on a shared branch.
            git reset --hard <hash>
            Throw history away back to that point. Only on a branch nobody else has.
            git rm --cached .env
            Stop tracking a file you should never have committed. Prints rm ‘.env’. The file stays on your disk.

            First time in a new project

            git init
            Start tracking this folder. “Initialized empty Git repository…”
            .gitignore
            Create it before the first commit. Minimum: node_modules/, .DS_Store, dist/, .env.
            git remote add origin <url>
            Point it at the empty GitHub repo. Silent.
            git push -u origin main
            First push. The -u is why every later push is just git push.
            README.md
            What it is, how to run it. GitHub shows it first, so it is the front door.

            Repo must be public
            On the free plan, Pages only serves a public repository. That is the rule that catches people.

            Source: Deploy from a branch. Branch: main, folder / (root).

            Create package.json without being asked twelve questions.
            npm install
            Install everything package.json lists. Creates node_modules/ — which is never committed.
            npm install name
            Add one package. Ask first whether you need it.

            Images and sounds go here, not next to your code. Anything else is not copied into the build.

            base:
            In vite.config.js. '/' for username.github.io; '/repo-name/' for a project repo. Wrong value = blank page and 404s in the console.

            The four errors, and what each means

            SyntaxError
            Your code is not valid JavaScript, so nothing ran at all. A missing bracket, brace or quote — usually a line or two above where it is reported.
            ReferenceError: x is not defined
            A name that does not exist. A typo, a missing declaration, or a variable whose scope has ended.
            TypeError: cannot read properties of undefined
            The commonest of all. You reached through something that was not there. The message names the property — look for what should have produced the value on its left.
            TypeError: x is not a function
            You called something that is not callable. A misspelt method, a missing await, or the wrong kind of value entirely.
            Every time
            Copy the literal error text, minus your own variable names, into a search engine. Hundreds of thousands of people have hit it.
